podcast.title: Formation and Sound
podcast.body: This group originated with Tim Armstrong, who was experimenting with computer-generated hip-hop beats. Travis Barker joined as the final piece of the band, allowing him to explore more demanding drumming parts than he typically played with Blink 182. It's described as an indie punk supergroup. "Travis had his own muses to follow. He and Tim Armstrong from Ranset got together to explore hip-hop beats in a group called the Transplants."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

podcast.title: Travis Barker's Artistic Stretch
podcast.body: Travis Barker appreciated the opportunity to stretch himself musically with The Transplants, learning to play drum parts that were significantly more demanding than those required in Blink 182. "Travis Barker from Blink 182, who really love the idea of being able to stretch himself by learning to play parts that were much more demanding than what he was called on to do with Blink 182."

xref.title: Gas Mask Tattoo - Transplants Nod
xref.body: He sports a gas mask tattoo, which serves as a direct reference or "nod" to the band The Transplants, which he co-founded in 2002. "There's a gas mask tattoo that's a nod to the transplants of Anteiformed in 2002."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mark Hoppus's Isolation During Side Projects
xref.body: While Tom DeLonge and Travis Barker pursued side projects like Box Car Racer and The Transplants, Mark Hoppus "stayed on the sidelines quietly fuming," feeling betrayed that Tom had asked Travis to drum for Box Car Racer, a project that had an "old DIY vibe of early Blink." "Mark left the studio and wrote what he thought would be an instant rejection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
